title: Pedestal Down
description: A pedestal down lowers the entire camera vertically without changing its tilt. The descent stays on one axis: a calm drop through the same look, not a nod and not a crane swoop.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Return to human height after a high formal view, or sit the camera down to a child, a table, a wound. Because tilt is constant, the world does not bow; we simply stand lower in it.
It is the wrong tool when you must look down as you drop, or when the arm should swing over a railing. If pitch changes, you left the pedestal.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Translate on Y only. Keep tilt, and usually keep yaw.
Vertical parallax reverses the up-move: architecture climbs the frame. Prompt a pedestal down, camera lowering vertically, no tilt, a calm descent through the same axis.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it to return to human height after a high formal view. Concrete beat: from a chandelier's height down to the couple, still looking along the ballroom, not down at the floor.
Do not tilt to keep them in frame; change height instead.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: A Crane Down can arc, advance, and even hand off to a walk. A Tilt Down pitches from a fixed height.
Pedestal Up is the opposite column. Pedestal down sits the camera down while it keeps looking the same way.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: Barry Lyndon favors formal, measured height and locked geometry over swooping arms. 2001: A Space Odyssey again treats vertical station as a physical fact of the set.
Use them as tilt-locked descent grammar.

sections.title: Prompt it

blocks.text: Pedestal down on [Subject], camera lowering vertically, no tilt, a calm descent through the same axis. For motion: the camera lowers straight down on a pedestal, keeping tilt constant, settling onto [Subject].

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is a Tilt Down or Crane Down. The tell is a nodding horizon or a curved path over furniture.
The fix: straight drop, tilt frozen, end at the new eyeline.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Pedestal Down in film?
It is a straight vertical lowering of the camera with tilt unchanged, so the lens occupies a lower station without nodding.
Pedestal Down vs Crane Down
Crane down travels on an arm and often changes angle as it arrives. Pedestal down is a column drop: same pitch, new height.
When should I use Pedestal Down?
When rank or scale should change by sitting the camera down, not by looking down. Do not use it to dive at a face from a rooftop.
How do I prompt Pedestal Down for AI image or video?
Write camera lowers straight down on a pedestal, tilt constant, no arc. Name the start height and the settle.
